## Summary

When a completion-verified close commits but fails to obtain its `completion-verifier`
attestation, the CLI's **default (text) output** says nothing about it. It prints only:

    transitioned <id>: in_progress -> closed; unblocked: none

Split out of `rookie-fickle-hydra` (3e21-4c5b-3e0d-4e23) so that bug can stay scoped to its
proven root cause (a symbolic `--ref` resolved twice). This is the separate REPORTING limb.

## What already exists — this is a narrow residual, not the whole gap

Bug `silvern-dewy-damselfly` (f4cf-60b2-41c0-4843) already delivered the machine-readable
marker. `completion_signature {signed, cause, error}` — with the closed cause vocabulary
`signed` / `material_drifted` / `sign_failed` / `force_bypassed` — reaches:

- the library: `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:385-386` (`rebar.transition()` return)
- the CLI JSON branch: `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:637-638` (`--output json`)
- MCP `transition_ticket`, which forwards the library result

and a warning is written to stderr on both failure branches
(`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:363-372` for drift, `:383-392` for a signing error).

What is NOT covered is the **default text branch**, `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:641-647`,
which never inspects `result["completion_signature"]`. A human — or an agent reading the
success line and not stderr — sees an unqualified success.

## Why it still matters

The attestation is the durable evidence that the close was earned. Its absence propagates:
`src/rebar/llm/completion_child_gate.py:185-205` classifies a closed-but-uncertified child as
`uncertified` with the detail "its subtree is unattested, so the parent closes WITHOUT
certification" — so one silently unsigned child close costs its parent story/epic its
certification too. A reader who never learns the first close was unsigned cannot connect the
two.

## Explicitly NOT in scope: a nonzero exit code

`f4cf` recorded this decision and it stands. `docs/exit-codes.md` declares the contract frozen
as of the 2026-06-09 window, pinned by `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_exit_codes.py`, with the
table at `:158` fixing `transition` at 0/1/10 — a new code is additive-only in a future window,
a release decision. Reusing exit 1 would be actively harmful: agents read 1 as "the transition
failed" and re-run it, which then exits 10 (already closed), trading a silent loss for a louder
wrong answer. This ticket is about the text output only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] When `completion_signature` is present and `cause != "signed"`, the default text output
      names the outcome on the same success line (or an adjacent line) — the ticket closed AND
      whether it carries an attestation — verified by a test per cause in the vocabulary.
- [x] A close that signs normally, a non-close transition, and `idea -> closed` (which carries no
      `completion_signature` key at all) print exactly what they print today — verified by tests.
- [x] Exit code remains 0 on every path — verified by a test pinning that decision.
- [x] `--output json` output is unchanged.

## Found by

Root-cause investigation of `rookie-fickle-hydra`. That bug's own AC3 ("A close that cannot
obtain an attestation says so in its output") is already met for library / JSON / MCP consumers
and unmet only here, which is why the residual is split out rather than folded in.
